text:
emma: Quick note from tonight's perf runs dashboards for tenant Y spike CPU due to RBAC checks happening after joins. Short thread to propose incremental fix.

reza: TL;DR options?

emma: 1) capability tokens (signed, short-lived) used by UI to skip auth-joins when token covers resource set. 2) planner prefetch of allowed ids from a small permission-index service and rewrite filter to id IN (...) when small.

omar: Tokens are least invasive. Main concerns: revocation and cross-tenant safety.

iris: For revocation we can use short TTL (2m) + a per-tenant rev_version checked in redis. Redis hit should be <1ms; fallback if missing.

emma: Planner prefetch is the cleaner long-term approach. Prefetch operator returns either small id set or a coverage flag. If id set > threshold, planner keeps original plan.

reza: Rollout idea: implement token fast-path first for owner/admin flows, measure. Parallel spike for prefetch to see id-set sizes.

omar: Telemetry: token_used, fast_path_hit, rev_check_latency, prefetch_allowed_count, prefetch_mismatch_rate. Also add correctness sampling comparing fast path vs full auth-join on 1% queries.

emma: Action owners: reza - token prototype + perf test; omar - permission-index spike + sampling; iris - security review + KMS rotation notes. I'll coordinate canary tenants.

deploy-bot: New job queued: console-query-executor v2.1-canary. Add migration flag.

emma: Let's reconvene with spike numbers early next week. Keep the RFC open for planner-auth integration. :white_check_mark:
